**SurgeXXL 0.2.0** — Surge XT 1.3.4's synth engine as a native MPC OS instrument for the Force (MPC OS 3.x).

> **This is the fix for "SurgeXXL loads nothing / crashes MPC".** Every earlier version (0.1.0-0.1.3) failed at the very first step on a Force: MPC runs plugins with no `HOME` variable, Surge asked for it while starting, and no instance could be made (the crash log said `create: exception The environment variable HOME is unset or empty`). Fixed, and every offline test now runs without HOME, as MPC does.

Also new: built with the mpc-vst-plugins wrapper fix for Q-Links on the automation screen (UpdateDisplay, #486-#489).

Every Surge factory and third-party patch (3008) and wavetable (761), your own patches (SAVE) and wavetables (`/sdcard/SurgeXXL/Wavetables`), eight pages with Q-Links, every Surge effect except Spring Reverb (Airwindows included). See the README for the pages and folders.

## Requirements

- A first-generation MPC OS standalone device (32-bit ARM: Force, MPC Live / Live II, One, X, Key 61), **MPC OS 3.x** (the skin uses 3.x features).
- **Root shell access** (SSH) to the device, i.e. a modded unit. Installing plugins this way is unofficial: back up first, use at your own risk.
- About 450 MB free on `/sdcard` (the patches and wavetables).

## Install it on its own

The package is about 450 MB unpacked. Install routes unpack a package in the device's `/tmp`, which on a Force is held in RAM, so **install SurgeXXL by itself, not in a batch with other plugins**, and save your project first. The scripted install below unpacks on the card instead and doesn't use RAM:

1. Unzip, then copy the whole folder to the card: `scp -r SurgeXXL-0.2.0 root@<device-ip>:/sdcard/`
2. Run it: `ssh root@<device-ip> sh /sdcard/SurgeXXL-0.2.0/install.sh`
3. Remove the copied folder afterwards: `ssh root@<device-ip> rm -rf /sdcard/SurgeXXL-0.2.0`

The installer stops MPC, copies the plugin folder into `/sdcard/Synths`, backs up `MPC.settings`, adds SurgeXXL to MPC's plugin list and starts MPC again. Installing over 0.1.3 replaces it. From 0.1.2 or older (the `ANDREALPHEUS - VST - SurgeXXL` folder): run that version's `uninstall.sh` first, or delete that folder, so its 450 MB doesn't stay on the card. Your own patches and wavetables in `/sdcard/SurgeXXL` are never touched.

Then add **SurgeXXL** to a track from the plugin browser (Instrument plugins). To check it started: `cat /sdcard/SurgeXXL/surgexxl.log` ends with `ready: 3008 patches, 761 wavetables`.

## Uninstall

`ssh root@<device-ip> sh /sdcard/SurgeXXL-0.2.0/uninstall.sh` (copy the folder over again if you removed it).
